intro: Lesson 5: The Mughals in 1526: Babur and Humayun. To understand how Babur founded the Mughal Empire and why Humayun nearly lost it

questions.q: Give two reasons Babur won at Panipat.
questions.a: For example: guns and cannon; carts as a barrier with attacks from the sides
questions.model: Look at the diagram. Reason 1: guns and cannon frightened and broke the enemy. Reason 2: carts protected his centre while his horsemen attacked the sides.

questions.q: How long was Humayun in exile?
Core: Make a timeline of 1526 to 1556 with five events and one sentence of explanation each.
questions.a: 1526 Panipat; 1530 Babur dies; 1540 Humayun defeated; 1555 Delhi retaken; 1556 Humayun dies, Akbar rules
questions.model: Teacher shows the first entry: '1526: Babur defeats Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat using guns and clever tactics.'

questions.q: Extend: In the portal response box: 'Babur's victory was mainly due to technology.' How far do you agree?
questions.a: Balanced answer: guns mattered, but tactics, leadership and Lodi's weaknesses also counted

questions.q: Stretch: Why might the Mughal Empire have ended in 1540 if Humayun had not returned?
questions.a: Sher Shah's dynasty might have lasted; the Mughals had no base in India

questions.q: Big question: how did a prince who lost his kingdom go on to found an empire?
questions.a: Babur built a base in Kabul, then used guns, tactics and leadership to defeat the Sultan of Delhi at Panipat
